subject: Clarify.ai — prompt pack, recommended models & next steps for evaluation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clarify.ai>, Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@clarify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify.ai — prompt pack, recommended models & next steps for evaluation

Hi Samir / Clara —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can get you a focused eval slate next week: 

Summary of the call (2–3 bullets):
- Use case: Clarify.ai will convert long customer support threads (multichannel) into structured case summaries and suggested next actions; priority is accuracy on entity extraction and intent classification, with conservative tone for suggested replies.
- Data shape: average thread length ~6 messages (200–800 tokens), ~10% contain PII (customer phone, masked SSN), 3–4 domain-specific entities per case.
- Success signals: precision on entities >= 92% on labeled subset; high recall on intents for escalations (~95%); no major hallucination around billing/legal.

Red team / evaluation constraints:
- We will need a prompt set that includes heavy edge cases: chained references ("as mentioned above"), redacted PII ("[REDACTED]"), code snippets pasted in support messages, and ambiguous intents.

Recommended models to start (shortlist for evaluation):
- redwood/rlm-13b-q4 (dense, good latency for expected traffic) — primary candidate for generation + extraction probes
- open/ozone-7b-instruct (cheap baseline for sanity checks)
- redwood/rlm-34b-8bit (higher-quality gating model for escalations)

What we need from you to build the eval pack:
1) Prompt batch: a CSV with 200–300 anonymized user threads (raw text fields), and an extra column marking known sensitive tokens for redaction. If you can share a small sample (20–30 rows) today we can start a smoke-run.
2) Edge-case notes: short list of 8–12 categories you care about (examples above).
3) Priority intents + a few labeled examples (5–10 each) if available.

Attachments: Ive attached a template CSV (clarify_prompt_batch.csv) and a short eval checklist (eval-benchmarks-clarify.pdf).

Next steps — proposed timeline:
- You: sample CSV + edge-case list by Tue 2028-06-19
- Redwood: run smoke-run, return basic regression signal & recommended model config by Thu 2028-06-21
- Joint: schedule 30-min sync to review results week of 2028-06-24

Privacy / redaction note: when you provide samples, please leave PII masked (we accept [REDACTED] tokens) or provide a redaction map. If you prefer a secure transfer, we can provision a private S3 link (let us know).

Questions? Otherwise Ill expect the sample CSV and well queue a smoke eval.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify.ai — prompt pack, recommended models & next steps for evaluation

Thanks for the forward — ran a quick smoke-run this morning. High-level findings and immediate next steps:

Smoke-run results (summary):
- rlm-13b-q4: entity extraction precision ~90% on the 30-row sample, recall trailing at ~85% (edge cases around chained references and masked tokens are primary failure mode).
- ozone-7b-instruct baseline: lower precision (~82%), several hallucinations when asked to "infer missing contact info" (we respected [REDACTED] placeholder).
- latencies: rlm-13b-q4 median generation latency ~120ms per request on our dedicated test pool (good).

Immediate product/ops asks:
1) Priyom: confirm that Clarify is comfortable with a 48-hour hold for the sample in a private S3 we control with logging — we can auto-delete after 30 days on request and provide the audit log.
2) Neha: can you draft the short TTL process and retention note we can send to legal? We should include the audit log sample and S3 lifecycle policy snippet.
3) Marissa/ML: if we prioritize entity precision, recommended triage:
   a) add a lightweight rule-based post-filter for common entity patterns (phone, invoice ids) to recover precision quickly;
   b) run a targeted prompt engineering pass (context windows that include the last two messages only) to reduce chaining errors;
   c) keep rlm-13b-q4 as primary but gate escalations to rlm-34b-8bit for high-risk cases until we see stable precision.

Risks / regression notes:
- We saw a pattern where masked tokens in context made the model guess linkable fields; include an explicit instruction in prompt templates to "NOT hallucinate masked values" — we'll add that to the prompt pack.
- If Clarify plans to push more truncated threads (<=2 messages), the model recall drops sharply; suggest they surface such cases as an explicit bucket for evaluation.

Deliverables Ill push by EOD: short results deck (PDF), a sample prompt template with the non-hallucination guard, and a one-page ops TTL snippet.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
